item.title: Whose is this? Finding owners after class
item.explanation_text:
Class is over at the community center. There is a bag on the table. Ask “Whose bag is this?” to find the owner. Use whose before the name of the thing: whose bag, whose pen, whose book. If everyone can see the bag you mean, you can point to it and ask “Whose is this?”

If the bag belongs to you, you can say “It’s my bag” or “It’s mine.” Use my, your, her, our and their before a noun. Use mine, yours, hers, ours and theirs when the noun is already clear. For example, if Eva says “It’s my bag,” you can say “It’s hers.” If you speak directly to Eva, say “It’s yours.” If the bag belongs to you and your friend, say “It’s ours.” If it belongs to two other people, say “It’s theirs.”
item.contrast_text: Whose notebook is this? → Whose is this? | It’s my notebook. → It’s mine. | It’s your notebook. → It’s yours. | It’s her notebook. → It’s hers. | It’s our notebook. → It’s ours. | It’s their notebook. → It’s theirs.
item.common_error_pattern: Using a possessive pronoun before a noun, as in “mine bag,” or ending a sentence with a form that needs a noun, as in “It’s my.”

examples.bad: Whose is this pencil belongs to?

children.title: Claim a marker
children.instructions: You tell the teacher, “This is my marker.” Finish your short answer with one word.

children.title: Hand back a scarf
children.instructions: Mina tells you, “That’s my scarf.” Give it back to Mina and complete your reply with one word.

children.title: Check the water bottle
children.instructions: Lena says, “The blue bottle is mine.” She wants to know if the teacher found it. Use one possessive pronoun to complete the teacher’s answer.

children.title: Pick up a shared folder
children.instructions: The folder belongs to you and your class partner. Speak for both of you and finish the reply with one word.

children.title: Sort the brushes
children.instructions: Two classmates say, “These are our brushes.” Tell the teacher about the brushes. Use one word.

children.title: Fix a label for a name badge
children.instructions: The badge belongs to the person you are speaking to. Change one word and write the whole sentence.

children.title: Fix the reply about a ruler
children.instructions: Your classmate asks if the ruler is yours. It is. Change one word and write the whole sentence.

children.title: Point to a mystery item
children.instructions: Everyone can see the key you are pointing to. Ask the same question without naming the item. Start with “Whose” and end with “this.”

children.title: Give a shorter answer about a basket
children.instructions: The basket belongs to two classmates. Keep “The basket” at the start and replace “their basket” with one word.

children.title: Name the item in your reply
children.instructions: You are speaking to the owner of an umbrella. Start with “It’s” and end with “umbrella.” Keep the same owner.

children.title: Ask about a glove
children.instructions: You find a glove after class. Use every tile once to ask who owns it. Start with “Whose glove” and end with “this.”

children.title: Report who owns the cards
children.instructions: Two classmates tell you the cards belong to them. Use every tile once to tell the teacher. Start with “These cards.”
